=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:280-303 and 165-188 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The intake never extracts `failure_fingerprint` from the validated payload, and for `identical_failure_cap` reports the evidence after header stripping can yield `no-error-lines`.
  WHY: Two distinct cap-level failures share one heal lineage, so one can escalate past the lineage cap and block healing for the other, same as the header-collision bug fixed by this PR.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The PR description claims "unrelated review/autofix failures no longer share one fingerprint" as the dedup goal. The cap report class (`identical_failure_cap`) continues to collapse unrelated failures onto one heal fingerprint after this PR: after the four-line header is stripped, cap evidence (e.g. `identical_failure_cap: 3 identical review/autofix failures`, `repeated failure_reason=...`, `failure_fingerprint=...`) matches none of `error_signature`'s `_SOFT_LOG_PATTERNS` / `_SIGNATURE_PATTERNS` alternation (lines 218-222, 197-201 in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`), so every cap report yields the same `no-error-lines` signature, and `fingerprint("review_autofix", "autofix:identical_failure_cap", "no-error-lines")` is identical across cap reports regardless of the underlying failure. The intake extracts the payload's `failure_fingerprint` nowhere (`scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:165-188` reads every other payload field but not `failure_fingerprint`); the reporter already emits and validates it (`scripts/workflow_failure_heal_autofix_report.sh:61`, `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:590-592, 830-831`), and Copilot's inline review (comment id 4155958713 on `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:290`) explicitly recommends preferring that field for cap reports.
  Expected change site: `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh` around lines 280-293 (the `autofix_failure` signature branch), conditioned on `FAILURE_REASON == identical_failure_cap` — prefer `$(jq -r '.failure_fingerprint // empty' "${PAYLOAD_FILE}")` (validated as 64 hex by `validate_payload`) as the signature material, falling back to the current `error-signature --strip-autofix-header` output when absent.
  Evidence of absence: The PR's diff to `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:283-293` only adds the `--strip-autofix-header` flag. No hunk reads `.failure_fingerprint` from the payload, no `if [ "${FAILURE_REASON}" = "identical_failure_cap" ]` branch exists, and the new regression test `test_intake_autofix_fingerprint_ignores_reporter_header_lines` (`tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:1661-1687`) only models a non-cap `editor_empty_noop` payload — there is no cap-report regression test exercising two distinct cap `failure_fingerprint` values producing distinct heal fingerprints. The cross-pollination summary records the same gap from four pass-1 reviewers (deepseek, minimax, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen). The PR is scoped to the header issue per its title and "## Changes" section, but the dedup intent is not fully closed for cap reports.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: lines 181-187, 280-303; scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py lines 1486-1499 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The intake ignores the validated `failure_fingerprint` when fingerprinting `identical_failure_cap` reports. It derives the signature only from evidence after stripping the reporter header.
  WHY: Distinct cap failures therefore receive the same heal fingerprint; `budget_decision` can match an unrelated open issue or continue an unrelated closed issue’s lineage, suppressing a new heal attempt or escalating it.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh: 289-290 (the `autofix_failure` signature branch) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `identical_failure_cap` reports with different underlying failure fingerprints still produce the same heal fingerprint.
  WHY: Two unrelated cap reports from different PRs (different underlying failures, different `failure_fingerprint` values) produce the same heal fingerprint. The second report is filed as an occurrence on the first report's heal issue instead of opening its own, and the lineage is incorrect.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
